This local implementation replaces per-field effect ownership with one world
engine. It is one prerequisite of the complete field display query, not that

  record ("'`export_pcode/scripts/_-2c.pcode:237–339`).
- `_-2c._-8o`, `_-Z7` and `_-0S` append registrations, resolve the first name and
  unregister the first name, respectively. Removing a name is not removeChild.
  The old physical parent and the currently resolved name can therefore differ.
- `_-2c.Run` first collects every ready clip identity. `_‑9p` invokes its callback
  while attached, rereads the indexed completion record, removes through current
  layer-name resolution and then splices the record. A callback-created record

## Implementation and authoritative reads

`RegisteredEffects` separates concrete top/bottom/screen layer instances, ordered
name registrations, actual ordered children and ordered completion records.
`parent(clip)` and `owned(layer)` read physical ownership. A bottom layer belongs
to its actual field'"'s nested lower container; top/screen are World siblings.
Creating a next wrapper constructs its layer identities without registering them.
Reads do not create layers, move clips, draw random values or advance clocks.

"'`FieldRuntime.effects` and `.pending` are read-only compatibility snapshots of the
engine'"'s records. Their context field supports existing host observations; it is
not a physical parent or the source of the complete geometry population. Do not
build a field query by filtering those snapshots. The query must visit the actual
bottom layer's "'`owned` children under the wrapper'"'s retained transforms.

World polls one engine instead of filtering separate field arrays. It advances
registered host artwork once, keeps direct controller removal separate, and
clears old records before arrival's Deactivate/cache writes. Queue contents are
not display children and a global engine clear no longer silently overwrites
unprocessed queues in other wrappers. Artificial incoming-effect fixtures now
queue requests explicitly. Artificial gallery replacement explicitly detaches
and reattaches its retained clip objects instead of assigning a runtime array.

The source reread after a callback is intentional: saving an entry or filtering
into a replacement array can erase a newly created callback carrier. A changed
name resolution also cannot silently detach a child from a different parent.

its independent artwork tail continues.

## Implemented owner and read boundary

`World.fieldDisplays` owns a `FieldDisplays` model keyed by the actual `Field`
object in a WeakMap. Every construction receives fresh numerical identities,
including a revisit to the same coordinates. `FieldCache` continues storing
actor references and saved scalars; it never stores/reuses this wrapper model.
No gameplay UID or RNG draw is used for display identities.

`read(field)` returns frozen numeric snapshots of the root, all eight authored
slot instances and their authored descendants, tutorial identity/parent/stopped
source frame, concrete bottom117, stage-update counts, sizing requests and
collapse state. Construction clones every matrix/color array into independent
instance state; no `AssetPack`, `SwfClip`, cached `DisplayPlacement`, Pixi or DOM
object is retained or mutated. Reads never create instances, advance clocks,
resolve geometry, consume randomness, change parents or modify revisions.

The first tutorial is a root child after the eight authored slots. Later guides
are in the actor slot after its transparent helper and before subsequent actor
births. The selected frame is retained, independent of later writes to a map
record or `Field.tutorial`. Authored helper/logo identities and mask ranges remain
present. `stageUpdates` counts actual attached stage notifications, including
orphans and paused Worlds. It is **not** a synthetic timeline frame or a freshly
reconstructed random pose; native clip playback remains the parent's composition
work. Detached ancestors and detached117 stop receiving these notifications.

The authored1540 under-effects slot and nested117 bottom instance have distinct
identities. Bottom attaches at `_‑L9` and detaches at `_‑4j`; it is independent of
pending requests and attached effect membership. Parent effect ownership should
compose its actual registered lower-layer handle under these identities, rather
than copying `runtime.effects` or `effectQueue` into the wrapper's children.
Actor and life slots likewise expose explicit future owner insertion points;
the model does not infer actors/pickups from damage/Run arrays.
